scheme_name: Madho Singh Bhandari Cooperative Collective Farming Scheme
description:
The Madho Singh Bhandari Cooperative Collective Farming Scheme was launched by the Government of Uttarakhand on 1st April 2021. 

This scheme is named after Madho Singh Bhandari, a prominent figure in the state's agricultural history. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to promote cooperative farming among small and marginal farmers. 

The government aims to enhance agricultural productivity and improve the livelihoods of farmers through collective farming practices. 

The scheme targets small and marginal farmers who own less than two hectares of land. 

The initiative seeks to form cooperative societies that will enable farmers to pool their resources. 

The government has set a target to establish at least 1,000 cooperative societies under this scheme by the end of 2025. 

Each cooperative society is expected to comprise a minimum of 10 farmers. 

The benefits of the scheme include access to modern farming techniques and technologies. 

Farmers will also receive training in sustainable agricultural practices. 

The government will provide financial assistance of up to INR 5 lakh per cooperative society. 

This financial assistance is aimed at supporting the initial setup costs of the cooperative. 

Additionally, the scheme includes provisions for providing high-quality seeds and fertilizers to the farmers. 

Farmers will also have access to credit facilities through government banks and financial institutions. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a resident of Uttarakhand. 

Farmers must also belong to a cooperative society that is registered under the Uttarakhand Cooperative Societies Act, 2003. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested farmers must form a cooperative society with a minimum of 10 members. 

Next, they must register their cooperative society with the Registrar of Cooperative Societies in Uttarakhand. 

After registration, the cooperative society must submit an application for financial assistance. 

The application must include details such as the number of members and the proposed farming activities. 

Required documents include identity proof of members, land ownership documents, and the registration certificate of the cooperative society. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the Department of Agriculture, Uttarakhand. 

The department will conduct an assessment of the proposed farming activities. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed to the cooperative society's bank account. 

The disbursement is expected to occur within 30 days of approval. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of regular monitoring and evaluation. 

The Department of Agriculture will conduct periodic assessments of the cooperative societies. 

This will ensure that the funds are being utilized effectively for the intended purposes. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crore for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2021-2022. 

This budget is expected to support the establishment of approximately 1,000 cooperative societies. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote cooperative farming in India. 

Cooperative farming has been recognized as a viable solution to address the challenges faced by small farmers. 

These challenges include land fragmentation and lack of access to resources. 

The scheme aims to empower farmers by providing them with a platform to work together. 

By pooling resources, farmers can achieve economies of scale. 

This will lead to increased productivity and better market access. 

The government also aims to promote organic farming practices through this scheme. 

Farmers will be encouraged to adopt sustainable agricultural methods. 

This aligns with the national goal of promoting environmental sustainability in agriculture. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall economic development of rural areas in Uttarakhand. 

By improving the livelihoods of farmers, the scheme aims to reduce poverty in these regions. 

The cooperative model also fosters community development and social cohesion. 

Farmers will have the opportunity to share knowledge and experiences through the cooperative. 

This collaborative approach is expected to enhance innovation in farming practices. 

The government has also planned awareness campaigns to promote the scheme among farmers. 

These campaigns will provide information about the benefits and application process. 

The Department of Agriculture will organize workshops and training sessions for interested farmers. 

The scheme is expected to have a positive impact on food security in the state. 

By increasing agricultural productivity, the scheme aims to ensure a stable supply of food. 

The government is committed to supporting the agricultural sector through various initiatives. 

The Madho Singh Bhandari Cooperative Collective Farming Scheme is a significant step in this direction. 

It reflects the government's recognition of the importance of cooperative farming in rural development. 

The scheme is expected to empower farmers and transform the agricultural landscape in Uttarakhand. 

In conclusion, the Madho Singh Bhandari Cooperative Collective Farming Scheme is a comprehensive initiative. 

It aims to promote cooperative farming among small and marginal farmers in Uttarakhand. 

With specific financial assistance and support for modern farming techniques, the scheme has the potential to improve the livelihoods of many farmers. 

The focus on sustainability and community development further enhances its significance. 

Farmers interested in this scheme should take proactive steps to form cooperative societies and apply for assistance. 

The government is dedicated to ensuring the success of this initiative through regular monitoring and support. 

This scheme is a vital component of the broader efforts to strengthen the agricultural sector in India.
